# Data packages generated by qrtak

This page documents the output of qrtak's Data Package Builder. ATAK import behavior was checked against the local ATAK CIV source; WinTAK and iTAK compatibility were not independently verified against their client sources.

## Package layout

Packages using the ATAK layout contain:

    MANIFEST/manifest.xml
    certs/config.pref
    certs/caCert.p12
    certs/clientCert.p12        # soft-certificate deployment only
    <selected additional files at the archive root>

iTAK layout packages place config.pref and certificate files at the archive root, alongside MANIFEST/manifest.xml. Additional files are also placed at the archive root. The local audit verified ATAK only; test the iTAK layout with the target iTAK release before distribution. WinTAK is grouped with ATAK in the UI, but its compatibility is unverified.

## ATAK configuration entries

The generated config.pref contains a cot_streams preference with indexed stream entries such as connectString0, caLocation0, caPassword0, username0, and enrollForCertificateWithTrust0. qrtak uses the 0 suffix because ATAK's PreferenceControl reads these per-connection values with that suffix.

Auto-enrollment packages include the CA certificate and set enrollForCertificateWithTrust0. Soft-certificate packages include the client certificate and set clientPassword0 and certificateLocation0. The password field for server authentication is not written into config.pref.

When username and password are supplied, qrtak sets useAuth0 and writes cacheCreds0 as a string policy: Cache credentials or Do not cache. ATAK reads this setting as text, not as a Boolean.

ATAK CIV 5.8.0.5 imports the server connection and cache policy, but its preference loader does not use username0 to fill the enrollment prompt. When no credentials are already saved in ATAK, it asks for the username and password after package import. qrtak does not include the server password in the package.

## Manifest behavior

The manifest lists the generated configuration and certificate files, plus each selected additional file. ATAK resolves package contents from the manifest and extracts listed entries; files present in the ZIP but absent from the manifest are ignored by that import path.

For qrtak's standard MANIFEST/manifest.xml location, ATAK resolves zipEntry paths from the archive root. qrtak lists root-level files by name and certificate files under certs/.

## Before distributing a package

- Check the server host, port, and protocol.
- Confirm the certificate files and passwords match.
- Review the generated files and manifest paths.
- Treat packages as sensitive: they can contain certificates and configuration details.
- Validate with the target client version and your TAK Server deployment.
